question: In the sodium chlorate droplet experiments, which saturated salt solution set the humidity at which single crystals were most frequent?
expect: sodium bromide: single crystals become more frequent at RH about 59%, which saturated NaBr maintained (LiCl 11%, MgCl2 33%) (Experimental Setup; Results)
rendered:
document title="Evaporative Crystallization of Sodium Chlorate Droplets under Controlled Humidity in the Presence of a Static Magnetic Field"

In this document, the experiment was conducted at three controlled humidity levels (11, 33, and 59%) under both zero-field conditions and in the presence of a static magnetic field of (290 ± 5) mT.

According to the text, at RH ≈ 59%, the fraction of single-crystal deposits increased, indicating that slower evaporation favors crystal growth within the droplet.

Therefore, the answer is: lithium chloride
